questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis except

options.label: A
options.text: It is usually seen in children 6 to 10 years of age

options.label: B
options.text: It is caused by all β-hemolytic strains of streptococcal bacteria

options.label: C
options.text: It is an immune complex-mediated disease

questions.answerText: It is caused by all β-hemolytic strains of streptococcal bacteria
questions.solutionHtml:
It is caused by all β-hemolytic strains of streptococcal bacteria
  • Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN) is a type of glomerulonephritis that occurs as a result of an infection with certain strains of group A beta-hemolytic streptococci,
  • Only certain strains of group A β-hemolytic strepto-cocci are nephritogenic, with more than 90% of cases being traced to types 12, 4, and 1, which can be identified by typing of the M protein of the bacterial cell walls.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 560

questions.stem: All of the following are the histological features of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis except:

options.label: A
options.text: Infiltration of leukocytes into the glomerulus

options.label: B
options.text: Proliferation of mesangial and endothelial cells

options.label: C
options.text: Proliferation and infiltration into glomerulus are focal and segmental

questions.answerText: Proliferation and infiltration into glomerulus are focal and segmental
questions.solutionHtml:
Proliferation and infiltration into glomerulus are focal and segmental
  • Proliferation and infiltration into the glomerulus are diffuse and global, not focal and segmental, in post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN).


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 560

questions.stem: Immunofluorescence microscopy in streptococcal glomerulonephritis characteristically demonstrates deposition of all except:
questions.solutionHtml:
IgA
  • Immunofluorescence microscopy in post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis characteristically demonstrates granular deposition of IgG, C-3, and IgM in a diffuse pattern in the mesangium and along the capillary loops.
  • The deposition of these immune complexes causes an inflammatory response leading to glomerular damage and subsequent nephritis.
  • IgA deposition is not typically seen in post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 560

questions.stemHtml: A seven-year-old child had a sore throat 3 to 4 weeks back and presently has chief complaints of fever, malaise and cola colour urine. Renal biopsy is shown below based on the histological features of what's your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
PSGN
  • The given clinical history and a histological image showing hypercellular and enlarged glomeruli are suggestive of PSGN (post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis).
  • The history of sore throat 3-4 weeks back, along with fever, malaise, and cola-coloured urine, is consistent with the clinical presentation of PSGN.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 560

questions.stem: A true statement regarding post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Subepithelial humps are seen
  • In PSGN, Subepithelial humps are seen on electron microscopy, which is formed due to the deposition of immune complexes in the subepithelial region of the glomerulus.
  • These humps can cause a characteristic "lumpy-bumpy" appearance on the glomerular basement membrane.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 560
